feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. What I had to do in the controller: wheel radius sets turn rate per unit PWM difference, so going from 0.030 to 0.025 m lowers effective steering gain by about 17 percent. I raised kp from 0.8 to 0.96 to match it, and kept kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction. Evidence: iteration 9 (0.035 m, kp 0.7) scored 64.78, with oval progress rising from 0.227 to 0.273 and s-bend progress falling from 0.194 to 0.078 and slalom from 0.126 to 0.125 (slalom roughly flat). Every run still ends with max_error 0.060 to 0.067 m and RMS 0.019 to 0.036 m, so the peak is a bend transient. Decision rules for the next race: if the score is above 73.33 with s-bend and slalom progress recovering, the smaller wheel is helping bends, so try wheel_radius 0.022 m next. If the score falls while oval progress drops below about 0.20, the ground speed loss is the limit, so return to 0.030 m and test sensor_size 0.016 m. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.18 on the s-bend or slalom, the kp match is too high, so change kp in the controller, not the geometry.
requested_changes: If wheel_radius 0.025 m beats 73.33 with s-bend and slalom progress above the iteration 7 values, try wheel_radius 0.022 m with kp scaled to about 1.1. Iteration 9 (0.035 m) showed larger wheels cut bend progress (s-bend 0.194 to 0.078), so the bend trend points toward smaller wheels.

If wheel_radius 0.025 m falls below 73.33 while max_error stays at 0.060 to 0.067 m, return to wheel_radius 0.030 m and try sensor_size 0.016 m on the 80 mm row. The slalom has shown 2.0 line-loss events in most runs, and a larger footprint keeps readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold longer (unproven; iteration 1 changed sensor size with other variables).

If the smaller wheel lowers oval progress below about 0.20 while max_error is unchanged, try mass 1.1 kg at wheel_radius 0.025 m. Mass peaked near 1.0 kg (1.2 kg scored 60.1), so 1.1 kg is a narrow test of whether the optimum sits slightly above 1.0 kg.
